title: MarketPosition
description: The AUTHORED commercial positioning of a book BEFORE it is opened (Market Positioning DSL, roadmap 4.5). Like the Novel Brain it is an authored input the strategist writes by hand, so it lives under sources/ (sources/market-position.yaml), NEVER under registry/facts/ or registry/derived/ — it is neither a story fact (ADR-006) nor a recomputed projection (ADR-008). Where the Novel Brain declares the CREATIVE constitution (mission/voice/promise), the Market Position declares the COMMERCIAL thesis: who the target reader SEGMENT is, which genre TROPES the book leans on vs subverts, and the concrete COMMERCIAL PROMISE (pay trigger / first-30-chapter hook / 100-chapter sustainability). The roadmap's reader-segment / trope-map / commercial-promise concepts are the three sub-blocks below — each populated by the author and read by the pre-book admission check, so none is a stub. It is the INPUT to the deterministic market-admission verdict (market-admission.schema.json), which folds it with the Brain and the derived Market Snapshot. Advisory — authoring/validating it never gates (ADR-003).

channel.description: 男频 / 女频 / general — the platform channel this book is positioned for; matched against the Market Snapshot's channels.

reader_segment.description: The TARGET READER SEGMENT (roadmap 'reader-segment'). Who specifically this book is for, what pulls them in, and what makes them leave — sharper than the Brain's target_reader because it is a commercial admission decision, not a creative one.

primary.description: The core reader segment, e.g. '追爽的男频升级读者' / '吃CP糖的女频甜宠读者'.

secondary.description: Adjacent segments the book can also capture.

pull_triggers.description: What makes this segment start AND keep reading (the appeal levers).

drop_triggers.description: What makes this segment abandon the book (the churn risks to design against).

trope_map.description: The TROPE MAP (roadmap 'trope-map'). Which familiar genre tropes the book LEANS ON (comfort/expectation) vs which it SUBVERTS (differentiation). A book that leans on everything is generic; one that subverts everything is unsellable — the mix is the positioning.

leans_on.description: Tropes deliberately embraced to meet reader expectation, e.g. 废柴逆袭 / 扮猪吃虎.

subverts.description: Tropes deliberately twisted to differentiate, e.g. '金手指有代价' / '反派不降智'.

differentiation.description: The one-line answer to 'why THIS book and not the 100 like it' — the core differentiator.

commercial_promise.description: The COMMERCIAL PROMISE (roadmap 'commercial-promise'). The concrete money thesis: the pay trigger, the first-30-chapter hook that earns the subscription, and the 100-chapter sustainability that earns the long read. These are exactly the questions the pre-book admission check scores.

pay_trigger.description: The specific moment/mechanic that converts a free reader to a paying one (付费点).

first_30_hook.description: Why a reader opens chapter 2..30 — the front-loaded hook that earns the subscription.

sustainability_100.description: Why the book still has fuel at chapter 100 — the long-arc engine (升级线/悬念线/情感线) that prevents 后劲不足.

comparables.description: Comparable successful titles this positioning is benchmarked against.
